description:
Looking to join a world-class blockchain development team? Ava Labs makes it simple to deploy high-performance solutions for Web3, led by innovations on Avalanche. The company was founded by Cornell computer scientists, who partnered with Wall Street veterans and early Web3 leaders to execute a promising vision for redefining the way people build permissionless networks. Ava Labs is redefining the way people create value with Web3. Join us as we empower people to easily and freely digitize all the world’s assets on one open, programmable blockchain platform.

About the Role

As a Senior Engineering Manager, you will lead the AvalancheGo node team (Snowman consensus, P-Chain and validator management, networking, VMs, database and storage) and the EVM team (C-Chain/coreth, Subnet-EVM, libevm). This is a player-coach role: your time will be spent leading and growing the team, whilst being hands-on: reviewing consensus, networking, state and EVM changes, writing and challenging design docs and ACPs, and joining the incident rotation. You will own the network upgrade release train, partner with Product, Research, Security and DevRel to turn the protocol roadmap into quarterly plans that ship, and grow the next generation of Tech Leads and Staff Engineers.

Team: AvalancheGo & EVM
Reports to: VP of Engineering
Location: Remote - US; Hybrid - if located in NYC

What You'll Do

  • Manage and mentor the AvalancheGo and EVM teams; develop Tech Leads and Staff Engineers and build a promotion pipeline.

  • Own the network upgrade release train — versioning, release candidates, changelogs, backward compatibility, and communication with validators and exchanges — shipping every upgrade with clean testnet and mainnet activation.

  • Stay hands-on (30–40%): review PRs on consensus, networking, state and EVM paths; write and challenge design docs and ACPs; join the incident rotation.

  • Partner with Product, Research, Security and DevRel to turn protocol roadmap goals (validator and L1 features, interoperability, performance) into quarterly plans that ship.

  • Set measurable targets for node performance (bootstrap time, state sync, block throughput and latency), and keep libevm close to upstream geth with a known, bounded merge lag.

  • Run a blameless incident process and raise engineering quality across the codebase: test coverage, fuzzing, e2e and load tests, and benchmark regression gates in CI.


What You'll Bring

  • 10+ years of software engineering experience, including 4+ years managing engineers — some of it as a TLM or player-coach who still reviewed and shipped code.

  • Recent production Go (or Rust/C++ with a clear path to Go) in systems code — consensus, networking, storage or runtime paths — with profiling and benchmarking experience.

  • Experience leading teams building blockchain nodes or clients, consensus or replication systems, databases or storage engines, or similar high-correctness infrastructure.

  • Strong grounding in distributed systems: BFT and probabilistic consensus, finality, liveness and safety trade-offs, and adversarial networking.

  • Working knowledge of the Ethereum execution layer (state database, trie, transaction pool, gas accounting); direct client work is a strong plus.

  • A record of shipping software other people run in production: versioned releases, backward compatibility, public changelogs, and test strategies for critical systems.

  • Proven ability to lead and retain Staff and Principal-level engineers, and to run a distributed, async team with clear written planning and performance processes.

  • Soft skills:

  • Credibility with senior ICs: earns the room with technical judgment, and knows when to defer to the engineer who owns a system.

  • Writing-first communication and calm under incident pressure — clear decisions during a live network issue, a blameless follow-up after.

  • Direct coaching and ownership: gives honest feedback, sponsors people for promotion, raises risk early, and builds an inclusive culture across time zones.


Nice to Have

  • Hands-on experience with Avalanche or deep familiarity with another L1/L2 node codebase (geth, reth, Erigon, Cosmos SDK/CometBFT, OP Stack, Substrate, or similar).

  • Rust — parts of our storage stack (Firewood) are written in Rust.

  • Experience maintaining a fork of a large upstream project (such as geth) and keeping it in sync.

  • Open-source contributions, public speaking, or writing in the blockchain community.

WHY AVA LABS?

Ava Labs builds Avalanche, the blockchain platform institutions use to bring finance onchain. Since Avalanche launched in 2020, we have helped exchanges, banks, asset managers and fintechs move from experiments to live products, from tokenized funds and private credit to stablecoin payments and, now, the clearing and settlement ledger for the NYSE’s upcoming tokenized securities platform. Avalanche lets institutions run their own purpose-built networks with the performance, costs and participation controls they need, while staying connected to a broad ecosystem of DeFi protocols, liquidity and developers.

We are a team of experts in engineering, finance, economics, product and law, headquartered in New York City. You will work alongside people who have built at leading banks, exchanges and crypto companies, with the scope to shape how capital markets move onchain over the next decade. Ava Labs is backed by investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Polychain Capital and Initialized Capital.

Ava Labs is committed to diversity in the workplace and we’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not hire on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, citizenship, age, disability, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, parental status, sex, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, or any other basis protected by local, state or federal law. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business need.
